description: A graduate student is entering a new research area and needs a living map of papers, methods, datasets, unresolved questions, and recurring debates instead of a pile of disconnected reading notes.

user_profile.context: The reading list is growing quickly, but understanding is not yet accumulating in a usable way
user_profile.communication_style: Curious and systematic, likes seeing how ideas connect

fact_sheet.fact: The graduate student building the research map is named Elara Vance.
Elara Vance is a first-year PhD student in the Department of Cognitive Robotics at Aethelburg University.
Elara's primary research goal for the first year is to establish foundational understanding in the Dynamic Human-AI Collaboration subfield.
The unfamiliar subfield Elara is exploring is 'Dynamic Human-AI Collaboration in Autonomous Systems' (DHACAS).
The DHACAS subfield focuses on real-time adaptive interactions between humans and AI agents in complex, unpredictable environments.
A core debate in DHACAS concerns the optimal level of AI autonomy in safety-critical applications, specifically between 'full control transfer' and 'human-in-the-loop oversight'.
One foundational paper Elara is analyzing is 'The Algorithmic Trust Model for Adaptive Teaming' by Dr. Kaelen Thorne, published in 2019 in the Journal of Autonomous Systems.
Another critical paper is 'Cognitive Load Metrics in Human-AI Joint Decision-Making' by Dr. Linus Corvus, published in 2021, which introduces the 'Corvus-Index'.
Elara has identified 47 core papers published between 2018 and 2023 that are central to the DHACAS subfield.
The 'Synergy Framework Manifesto', published in 2018 by the 'Aethelburg Collective', is considered the seminal work that defined the DHACAS subfield.
A prominent methodology in DHACAS research is 'Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback' (RLHF), particularly for training adaptive AI agents.
Many studies in DHACAS utilize 'Scenario-Based Simulation' with human participants to evaluate joint decision-making under stress.
Eye-tracking and galvanic skin response (GSR) are common physiological data collection methods used to measure human cognitive load in DHACAS experiments.
The 'Aethelburg Human-AI Interaction Corpus (AHIC-2022)' is a publicly available dataset containing 1,500 hours of annotated human-AI interaction logs.
The 'Corvus Lab Simulation Outcomes' dataset, version 3.1, contains performance metrics from 500 simulated missions involving human-AI teams.
The 'Thorne Trust Calibration Dataset' (TTC-2020) provides human trust scores for 12 distinct AI agent behaviors across 300 participants.
One key unresolved question is how to quantify and predict 'human-AI team fluency' beyond task completion rates.
The debate around 'explainable AI (XAI)' in DHACAS centers on whether AI explanations should prioritize transparency, interpretability, or trust-building.
Researchers are still debating the ethical implications of AI agents learning to 'persuade' human operators in critical decision-making scenarios.
Elara uses Zotero for reference management, with a specific collection named 'DHACAS Core Literature' containing 112 entries.
Obsidian is Elara's chosen tool for building the 'living map' of interconnected notes and ideas, utilizing its graph view for visualization.
The primary programming language used for DHACAS simulations and AI development in her department is Python, often with the PyTorch framework.
Elara's PhD advisor is Professor Dr. Seraphina Reed, head of the Human-AI Interaction Lab at Aethelburg University.
Professor Reed recommended Elara attend the 'DHACAS Annual Symposium' in October 2024 to network with key researchers.
Elara is assigned to desk W-07 in the graduate student office of the Cognitive Robotics department, located on the 3rd floor of the Turing Building.
Aethelburg University provides access to the 'Cognitive Science Research Portal' (login via portal.aethelburg.edu/csrp) for literature reviews.
The university library offers weekly workshops on 'Advanced Literature Mapping Techniques' every Tuesday at 10:00 AM in Library Room 210B.
Professor Seraphina Reed is known in this subfield for work on trust calibration and human-in-the-loop oversight in safety-critical human-AI systems.
Named contributors repeatedly appearing in Elara's DHACAS map include Dr. Kaelen Thorne, Dr. Linus Corvus, and the Aethelburg Collective.
Another unresolved question in DHACAS is how quickly human trust should be recalibrated after an AI error without causing either over-reliance or sharp distrust.
Researchers also disagree on whether DHACAS systems should optimize primarily for individual operator adaptation or for team-level coordination in multi-human settings.

Elara's literature map also repeatedly flags Professor Seraphina Reed and the Corvus Lab as central contributors on trust calibration, human oversight design, and cognitive-load evaluation methods in DHACAS.
